newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa jumps almost 5 pct, ends off peaks.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa jumps almost 5 pct, ends off peaks.

text.p: Cocoa futures leapt by nearly five percent on Tuesday to the highest since October in a blistering rally fuelled by panic fund buying and spec short-covering.
Late profit-taking took some of the heat off the market but values still finished sharply higher.
"This is expected as the market is overdone and overbought," said one. "Some suggested that it could pull back to 970 (stg) area."
Benchmark May, extending Monday's rally, soared to a high of 1,027 stg a tonne, a five-month high, before finishing the day 29 stg up at 1,010 stg.

Prices had opened at 998 stg against Monday's ceiling of 982 -- a chart gap of 16 stg -- and traders said there could be a possible one-day "island reversal" on the charts if London opens Wednesday above today's low of 997 on Wednesday.
Such a situation leaves price action looking like an "island" surrounded by space or water on the charts.

There was no new fresh fundamental news driving the rally and traders said the buying gained momentum as shorts decided to aggressively cover their positions. This sparked panic buying from the funds.
"The market has realised that there are sizeable shorts in the nearbys...the specs and the funds have gone long," said one.
"We have seen people going long in the market...at the moment it looks pretty constructive and I think there will be more buying to come."
Volume was a hefty 9,226 lots with May accounting for 4,051 lots.
Nearby structure remained tight with May/July spread holding at level money by the close.

The market saw a flurry of news on Monday with the main talking point was comments by a Phibro director Anthony Ward that he believed prices could hit 1,500 stg a tonne because of a structural deficit. Phibro is a major player in cocoa market.
There were also crop updates from key growers Ivory Coast and Ghana.

Broker GNI said in comments on Tuesday that while the dramatic rise in prices (on Monday) "was indicative of the markets initial vote from the Phibro comments, the rest seem to be an attempt to bolster prices."
"The question is what happens to prices if manufacturers successfully hold off for a while longer?"
Cocoa prices hit an eight-year-high of 1,172 stg last year on a supply squeeze as a major trader took delivery of 300,000 tonnes of cocoa. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
